target.title: fix: generic criterion matching returned nil for CF-typed attributes
target.body:
## Problem
`performGenericAttributeMatch` fetches the actual value via `element.attribute(Attribute<Any>(key))`, which returns nil for CF-typed values. Every generic criterion (`AXTitle`, `AXValue`, …) therefore never matched — e.g. `{AXRole: AXWindow, AXTitle: <exact title>}` failed even when the title matched exactly (verified: the same element's `AXTitle` was readable via `describeElement`).

## Fix
Read the raw attribute value (`rawAttributeValue(named:)`) first, falling back to the generic path.

## Verification
Before: `axorc find --app <SwiftUI app> --role AXWindow --title '<exact title>'` → FTE not-found. After: found. Test suite green.

target.title: fix: use AXUIElementCopyActionNames for supportedActions()
target.body:
## Problem
`supportedActions()` reads the `AXActionNames` attribute via `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue`. For SwiftUI apps this returns nothing, so `isActionSupported("AXPress")` is always false and every `performAction` fails with `Available actions: []`.

## Fix
Query the dedicated `AXUIElementCopyActionNames` API first, keeping the attribute read as a fallback.

## Verification
Reproduced against a SwiftUI app (AXPress on a plain `Button`): before the fix the action was rejected with an empty action list; after the fix the press succeeds. Full test suite still green (51 tests).
